correctness.rationale: Assign every vertex its unique firing phase mod p. For each phase configuration its allowable residual chip count is u_v in [0,a_v-1], with a_v the number of neighbors firing immediately before that vertex, so its number of time-zero microscopic states is exactly product_v a_v. Choosing these predecessors gives a functional digraph whose every directed cycle has length divisible by p. In a theta graph no two vertex-disjoint directed cycles exist; the unique directed cycle uses two complete terminal-to-terminal arms, in one of two orientations; the remaining arm has exactly its L_i acyclic pointing-to-terminal choices. The p global phase choices cancel temporal rotation, and unique single firing forces least period p. Independent exhaustive phase counts on theta(1,2,3) yield four period-4 and two period-5 temporal orbits and zero period-6, agreeing with formula. No general counting assertion relies on this finite sample.
residual_risks: Phase-state bijection assumes nonnegative integer chip counts and synchronous update; no result asserted for transient or higher-firing activity sectors.
